text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] decode-service/us-west-2 p99 latency breach 00:13 ago — p99=2.9s (SLO 1.2s), p95=1.1s. Spike coincides with deploy tag=trt-flashattn-v3.3. Auto-notify: #eng-sre and #eng-runtime.

oncall-eli: got the page, looking. Is this only decode nodes or also routing? seeing an increase in page-faults on the benchmarks host.

sato: I'm seeing the same on the dashboard — streaming stalls metric spike. tail_latency spike mostly for seq_len>1024. Likely kernel/compile path change in v3.3. @kira can you confirm kernel builds?

kira: deployed trt-flashattn-v3.3 at 03:10 UTC (canary->prod). The release switched to new CUDA kernel set and toggled compile flag "--enable-fma" in the release toolchain. I can roll back the canary in 5m.

oncall-eli: hold on rollback for a sec. Need quick mitigations: 1) divert traffic off decode-fleet-3 (highest tail) 2) enable legacy-kernel flag via runtime feature-flag 3) if that doesn't work, rollback.

matt: I'm running a query for customer impact — how many active requests hit the affected fleet in the last 15m. Running: `kql: logs "decode-worker" and host:decode-fleet-3 and latency>1000`

ops-sre: @matt hint: include `model_variant:*trt*` — we saw routing prefer trt variants after the optimizer change.

matt: result: 362 requests >1s in last 15m on decode-fleet-3, 24 unique customers, 3 high-volume streams. Top affected: cust-omega (30% of tails), cust-beta (12%).

oncall-eli: good. I'm going to patch the routing rule to reduce load on decode-fleet-3 by 60% (canary flow -> fallback to cpu-backend). Doing it now: `rbacctl route set decode-fleet-3 weight=0.4 --reason "emergency p99 mitigation"`

incident-bot: Change accepted. Routing change applied.

sato: after routing change, p95 dropped to 0.9s, p99 down to 1.8s but still above SLO. Streaming stalls count down ~40%.

kira: I'm flipping runtime feature `use_legacy_flash_kernel=true` on decode-fleet-3, will patch via console API. Command: `curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/flags -d '{"flag":"use_legacy_flash_kernel","hosts":["decode-fleet-3"]}'`

oncall-eli: do it, note if host needs restart.

kira: applied flag, no restart. Telemetry shows kernel selection moved back to legacy path for active sessions. p99 now 1.25s and falling.

matt: customers still seeing streaming stalls for long seqs (some sessions with stateful streaming saw KV cache invalidations when the kernel path changed). We should surface to CS. Patch note: short-lived stalls for sessions that migrated kernel mid-stream.

ops-sre: we need to root cause — is this a correctness bug in new kernel or resource pressure (paging)? I'm seeing increased minor page-faults and thrashing on cuda memory allocs during decode. Could be allocator change in the new build.

sato: adding kernel team: @kira @matt please run `nvprof` trace on a repro. Also capture `dmesg` and kernel logs for page faults.

kira: grabbing nvprof, attaching to small repro. Found large numbers of device->host syncs in the new kernel when sequence >1024, causing stalls. Looks like an unexpected fallback path in the FlashAttention kernel for long sequences.

oncall-eli: temporary mitigation summary for postmortem: - routing weight change (60% off) - legacy kernel flag - targetted host flagging (no restart) - notify customers; CS escalation for top 3.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV2 (customer-facing SLO breach). Owner: oncall-eli.

matt: CS notified: tickets created for cust-omega and cust-beta. Email templates attached.

ops-sre: for longer-term fix, kernel team needs to: 1) reproduce locally, 2) for FlashAttn kernel avoid device->host syncs on long sequences, 3) re-run compile with "--no-fma" and compare, 4) devise canary that exercises seq_len distribution.

kira: already reproduced. Hypothesis: the new CUDA kernels introduce an out-of-line fallback that does a host staging copy for >1024 tokens due to shared memory limits. On some hardware/driver combos that triggers extra page-faults and sync.

sato: are specific GPUs affected? I see NVSMI shows more remaps on A10 vs A100. Might be driver+cuda interaction. Which environments ran the v3.3 build? canary -> all prod us-west; some dedicated pools in eu-west also got it.

oncall-eli: action items (immediate):
- kira: create a 1-line rollback of trt-flashattn-v3.3 to v3.2 if legacy flag doesn't fully remediate (ETA 15m)
- matt: keep routing adjusted and re-run impact query every 5m (share dashboard snapshot)
- sato: collect nvprof traces + dmesg + allocator stats, upload to /shared/incidents/1867348290/
- ops-sre: coordinate with kernel team for a safe repro harness and driver matrix test

kira: ack. Starting rollback prep (not executing yet) — need thumbs from oncall.

oncall-eli: thumbs. If p99 >1.8s in next 10m enable rollback.

(devops-bot): deployment pipeline check: trt-flashattn-v3.3 was built with toolchain v2.14 and compiled with `-O3 -march=sm70 -ffast-math` flags. Previous v3.2 used `-O2 -march=sm70` and no fast-math.

ops-sre: that lines up — fast-math can change FP behavior and sometimes forces different code paths in attention kernels. Good call.

kira: for a less disruptive workaround we can rebuild v3.3 with `-fno-fast-math` and roll a patch canary in 30m. That avoids full rollback and keeps other improvements.

oncall-eli: prefer targeted rebuild if it reliably fixes. matt keep monitoring.

matt: 5m check: p99=1.18s, p95=0.85s. Still trending down. Customers with long streams report brief interrupted tokens but recovered. Dashboard snapshot: https://dash.redwood/s/incident/1867348290

sato: preparing postmortem notes: root-cause preliminary: new FlashAttn kernel with `-ffast-math` led to fallback device->host staging for long sequences on certain drivers causing increased page-faults and device syncs -> tail latency spikes.

oncall-eli: good. We'll keep incident open until 4h with status updates. Next: ship rebuild without `-ffast-math` as a canary then full roll.

incident-bot: Status update (00:30 elapsed) — mitigations applied, p99 within 5% of SLO, incident owner oncall-eli.

matt: closing note for CS: we offered credits to cust-omega and cust-beta and opened follow-ups.

ops-sre: logging next steps for postmortem and action items: add canary sequence distribution tests, add allocator metrics to perf dashboards, require driver matrix test for kernel releases.

oncall-eli: thanks team. I will hand this off to operations for the daytime shift at 04:00 UTC with a summary. End of thread for now.
